diagnosis_explanation: Your left kidney has a mass. It is called cancer. It is also called a cyst. Your lungs have a long-term problem. This problem makes it hard to breathe. Your heart has a problem too. It is called coronary artery disease. This means your heart's blood vessels are narrow.

recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and sore after your surgery.
- Keep activity light. Rest often.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 10 pounds.
- Drink plenty of fluids.
- Take pain medicine as prescribed.
- Your goal this week is to walk a little each day.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101.5.
- Call your doctor if pain is too bad to manage.

**Week 2:**
- Your energy levels may start to slowly improve.
- You can do more light tasks around the house.
- Avoid lifting anything heavy.
- Keep up with drinking fluids.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 5-10 minutes, twice a day.
- Call your doctor if you have nausea or vomiting.
- Call your doctor if you have any other concerns.

**Week 3:**
- You should feel less soreness and more energy.
- You can resume more normal daily activities.
- Continue to avoid heavy lifting.
- Drink fluids throughout the day.
- Your goal this week is to increase walking time to 15 minutes.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101.5.
- Call your doctor if pain is not getting better.

**Week 4:**
- You may feel much more like yourself this week.
- You can likely do most light chores.
- You can slowly return to normal activities.
- Keep drinking plenty of fluids.
- Your goal this week is to walk 20 minutes daily.
- Call your doctor if you have nausea or vomiting.
- Call your doctor if you have any other concerns.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Most people feel significantly better within 4 to 6 weeks.
- Healing is a gradual process.
- Continue to follow your doctor's instructions.
- Listen to your body and rest when needed.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Chest pain: Your heart needs help now.
- You cannot catch your breath: Your body needs oxygen now.
- Face drooping or arm weakness: These are stroke signs. Minutes matter.
- Uncontrolled bleeding: Apply pressure; it must stop.
- Unresponsive or passed out: Get help right away.
- Seizure: This needs urgent care.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever greater than 101.5: You may have an infection.
- Intractable pain: Your pain is very bad.
- Vomiting: You cannot keep fluids down.
- Any other concerns: Do not ignore worries.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Nausea: You may feel sick to your stomach.
